title: LLM Gateway Adaptor and Performance Contract Orchestrator: end-to-end community model onboarding
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a unified onboarding conduit (gateway adaptor + orchestrator) to intake community weights, run deterministic conversion and quantization, validate behavioral and perf contracts, produce a canonical pin, and publish performance profiles to the catalog. This ticket scopes the core orchestration, acceptance tests, and publishing hooks needed for a safe, auditable end-to-end flow for open-source LLMs. Goals: 1) make onboarding repeatable and reproducible; 2) ensure performance contracts (latency/cost/quality) are asserted before pin publication; 3) provide clear audit trail and rollbacks; 4) provide fallback mappings for runtime variants.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts signed manifests (S3/HF links) and verifies provenance signatures or alternate attestations
Automated conversion pipeline produces deterministic artifacts (float/quantized) with reproducible checksums
Variant matrix produced with kernel/quantization metadata and validated runtime compatibility list
Performance contract tests run: latency P95, throughput, token-cost estimate, and quality regression vs baseline prompts
Pin publish step creates immutable model pin and publishes profile JSON to model-catalog with provenance and perf-metrics
On failure, automatic rollback or quarantine path with human review notification
Integration tests and smoke harnesses triggered in staging and pass before release to prod catalog
steps: Design manifest schema update to include provenance/signature and optional provenance_url
Implement gateway adaptor to normalize HF/S3 manifests and enqueue into intake-orchestrator
Conversion job: run hf -> runtime-optimized format using deterministic seed and record conversion log
Run quantization matrix (int8/4bit paths) recommended by model profile heuristics
Execute validation suite: unit checks (shapes, ops), deterministic inference tests, and sample outputs for a 50-prompt smoke set
Execute performance contract suite in staged runtime pools: latency P50/P95, batching behavior, KV-cache warms, and cost per token estimate
Select canonical variant for pin based on contract pass + cost-quality tradeoff heuristics
Publish pin and profile to catalog and emit audit entry with links to artifacts and PR
Post-publish: schedule canary traffic to prod-hosted pool and monitor for regressions for 48h
comments: 2025-02-14 | Aisha Khan: Initial ticket created after scoping session with PM and runtime. Key requirement: deterministic conversion reproducibility for auditability.

risk: Medium. Risks include non-deterministic quantization side-effects, insufficient runtime kernel coverage for community models, and incomplete provenance leading to quarantine. Mitigations: add op-fallback rules, expand kernel compatibility matrix, and enforce provenance policy with manual override paths.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest normalization, deterministic checksum comparisons for converted binaries, regression tests on the 50-prompt smoke set, perf contract runner that emits pass/fail and metrics to the staging dashboard. End-to-end integration test runs nightly in staging with synthetic traffic to validate canary rollout behaviors.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge intake adaptor and conversion-runner to staging. 2) Onboard 3 low-risk community models (MIT/BSD licensed) behind feature flag. 3) Run perf contracts and publish internal-only pins. 4) After 7 days and 0 regressions, enable public catalog publish. 5) Monitor for 14 days with automated rollback on perf regression breach.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: we prefer deterministic conversion even if it means slower conversion time (longer CI step). For certain large models, an initial fast-path conversion will be allowed but will remain non-pinned until deterministic conversion completes. Need follow-up ticket to add automated license scanning for community weights.
